# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_013_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 5

**1** After I had written the book I was commanded in the former vision to write, the Spirit of God took me up and carried me away to a pathless land. **2** And immediately the Spirit was changed, and I was able to see the tower clearly, and around it were twelve mountains; each mountain had a different appearance. **3** The first mountain was black as soot. The second mountain was bare, with no vegetation. The third mountain was full of thorns and briars. The fourth mountain was full of herbs, half of which were withered at their tops while the other half were green. The fifth mountain had green grass and was quite rugged. The sixth mountain was entirely full of clefts, some larger and some smaller. The seventh mountain had cheerful vegetation, the whole mountain flourishing and all manner of cattle and birds feeding upon it; the more they fed upon it, the more the vegetation flourished. The eighth mountain was full of springs of water, and every kind of creature of the Lord drank from those springs. **4** The ninth mountain had no water at all, and it was entirely wilderness; in it were savage wild beasts and deadly serpents that destroyed men. The tenth mountain had great trees and was entirely shaded; under the shadow of those trees sheep were resting and ruminating. The eleventh mountain was thickly overgrown with trees, and those trees were laden with various fruits, so that anyone who ate of them desired to eat more. The twelfth mountain was entirely white, and its aspect was very joyful.

---

*EMET note: Vision 3, Chapter 5 presents the twelve mountains — a major new allegorical image. These mountains represent twelve different kinds/categories of people in the Church. Interpretation follows in subsequent chapters.*
